cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing a letter to Timothy, a disciple Paul brought along on his travels (Acts 16:1-3). He opens with grace, mercy and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord. Friend, that's not a hello, that's a whole CARE PACKAGE.

cards.question: Paul says he's an apostle of Christ Jesus. By whose command?

answers.text: God our Savior and Christ Jesus

cards.text: Paul calls Timothy his true child in the faith. As a Papa myself, friend, that line gets me right in the apron.
Then Paul gets down to business. When he left for Macedonia, he urged Timothy to stay on in one city.

cards.question: Which city did Paul urge Timothy to stay on in?
Timothy is supposed to instruct certain men in that city to stop doing something. What is it?

cards.text: These men are also hooked on myths and endless genealogies. ENDLESS, friend, like the dead batteries I shared that drawer with, arguing for YEARS over who had the most charge left.

cards.question: Paul says those myths and endless genealogies promote ___ rather than the stewardship of God's work.
What does Paul say is the goal of his instruction?

cards.text: Love that comes from a pure heart, a clear conscience and a sincere faith. But some people have strayed from all that and turned aside to empty talk.

cards.question: The people who turned aside to empty talk want to be teachers of the ___.
Paul says these would-be teachers of the law understand what they're saying.

cards.text: And they say it all so confidently. You know the type, friend: the guy in the group chat explaining traffic laws with his WHOLE chest who has never once driven a car.

cards.question: What does Paul say about the law itself?

answers.text: It is good if used rightly
It has been done away with
It is too heavy to carry

cards.question: Paul says the law is enacted for the righteous.

cards.text: The law is for the lawless and rebellious, and Paul keeps going down a long list: the ungodly and sinful, murderers, the sexually immoral, slave traders, liars and more. He ends it with anyone else who is averse to sound teaching.

cards.question: What does Paul say that sound teaching agrees with?

answers.text: The glorious gospel of the blessed God
The traditions handed down by the elders
The wisdom of the Greek teachers

cards.question: Paul says he has been entrusted with that glorious gospel.

findings.problem: The question refers to “that city” without naming Ephesus. Its referent appears only on earlier cards, so the question does not fully supply its own context.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The blank asks for the unseen wording “law,” but nothing in the earlier cards lets the baker reason that these people want to teach the law rather than the prophets or the psalms. This is a wording guess, not a test of meaning established by the setup.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Too many choices depend on recall or luck rather than reasoning from the earlier cards. Cards 9, 11, 15, 17 and 18 do not provide enough setup to establish their answers, while cards 2 and 5 are additional discovery questions. Discovery questions therefore make up too large a share of the stop for most choices to be informed guesses.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
